analysis: Reviewed ClusterService.swift (base lines 1315-1751 and head lines 1-487). The visible patch hunks only rewrite date comparisons: Date() >= x becomes Date().timeIntervalSince(x) >= 0 at lines 510, 646, 909, 1044, 1126 and 1582. These are behavior-equivalent for finite dates. The one nuance is Date.distantPast, which is used as the initial value of nextSync and nextMemoryReplan; timeIntervalSince(distantPast) is a large finite positive number, so those checks still pass. I found no security-relevant behavior change. The changes touch only restart backoff, sync cadence and memory-replan scheduling. None of them touches authorization, App Attest, the attestation chain, encryption, key handling, the WebSocket, the add-on hold socket (TB-012) or the prefix-cache storage (T-041). The available text shows no new file or process surface. Local-service lock, log and status files stay owner-only (0600 and private directories); this is unchanged from base. Limitations: the patch excerpt is truncated after the line 1044 hunk, and the head text covers only lines 1-487. The line 1126 and line 1582 head content was not visible. The base text for 1582 shows the same mayStart backoff comparison, and the range map says only those lines changed. I assume those two are equivalent mechanical rewrites. I checked no unchanged callers. The service's control-link authentication (pairing edge secret) is unchanged and outside the visible diff.
